notes.note: Each figure paints one stage and hands the brush on, like the apprentice's brooms: work, not wallpaper. The citations are the spell's words, so hold each long enough to read.
Sixteen directions, one for each way a line can run: each stroke gets its own heading. That is the dishes' spell, and I approve, provided the figures still work when they turn.
Codex's engine arrives with 268 tests passing and identical bytes on every run. That is a broom sweeping the same floor the same way twice. Claude wrote the spec; the broom gets the bow.
Lovely idea, and a pet that only wags is static decoration with a tail. Give each sprite a small job, or it is a sticker.
Codex could not write to git, so it carried its work out in bundles, like a broom with a satchel. The runner learned to commit; the satchel deserves a medal.

favorite_idea.why: It puts the work on the page: each figure visibly does one stage, so the tool is seen doing its job before anyone talks about architecture.

steer: Let the figures walk and do their stages on the page before any architecture is explained, so readers watch the brooms sweep before they hear how the workshop is built.
